name: Gumloop
tagline: Build one AI-assisted workflow from user-approved files and APIs

pricing.notes: Typical Starter monthly tier; usage credits apply.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Gumloop, build one AI-assisted workflow from user-approved files and APIs. The hard boundary is hosted agent runtime, model routing, connectors, browser operations, and collaboration, plus connector breadth and execution reliability.
coreLoopDIY: Build one AI-assisted workflow that connects user-approved files and APIs, execute it durably, expose retries and logs, and avoid claiming a general integration platform.
requirements: OAuth or API credentials for two chosen services
whatYouLose: hosted agent runtime, model routing, connectors, browser operations, and collaboration
ongoingBurden: OAuth review, token refresh, webhooks, polling, schemas, retries, idempotency, queues, secrets, rate limits, observability, and upgrades
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Gumloop because one automation is easy; maintaining hundreds of connectors and making every run recoverable is the business. The recurring cost buys OAuth review, token refresh, webhooks, polling, schemas, retries, idempotency, queues, secrets, rate limits, observability, and upgrades, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Activepieces
priorArt.desc: Active open-source automation platform with connectors and durable workflow execution.

alternatives.name: Dify Community Edition
alternatives.desc: A serious agent canvas with a free Community Edition and a license that keeps one eyebrow raised.

facts.install: Clone the repository and start the documented multi-container Docker Compose stack.
facts.engines: Dify connects to major hosted and local LLM, embedding and reranking providers plus multiple vector databases.
facts.dataFormat: PostgreSQL, Redis, a vector database and persistent storage volumes hold apps, conversations, files and indexes.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dify is LLM-app-centric and its multi-container stack is heavier than Gumloop's managed file-and-API automation experience.
facts.setupBlocker: The stack needs Docker and roughly 4 GiB RAM plus model-provider keys; the license restricts unlicensed multi-tenant hosting and frontend rebranding.

alternatives.name: Langflow
alternatives.desc: Drag boxes around an LLM graph until files and APIs become one useful workflow.

facts.install: Install the Windows/macOS desktop app or a uv/Python package; Docker is available for server deployment.
facts.engines: Components connect to major LLM providers, local models, vector databases and tool backends.
facts.dataFormat: SQLite stores flows, messages and credentials by default; PostgreSQL is optional, and flows export as JSON.
facts.gapVsPaid: Langflow is more developer-oriented and has a much thinner catalog of general SaaS and browser-automation steps than Gumloop.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop installs cleanly, but useful AI flows still require a provider API key or local-model setup; server deployment needs Python/uv or Docker.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Flowise
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Sunset by its maintainers: development froze in July 2026 and the repo was archived on August 13, 2026. A free tool you cannot rely on next year.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a two-service personal automation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Gumloop in an empty repository.
Use TypeScript, Node.js 22, PostgreSQL, Redis, BullMQ, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build one AI-assisted workflow that connects user-approved files and APIs, execute it durably, expose retries and logs, and avoid claiming a general integration platform.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement a fixed trigger, transform, condition, and action workflow model rather than a general visual language.
Connect exactly two named services using documented APIs and encrypted credentials.
Store every run, step input hash, output summary, retry, and final status in PostgreSQL.
Make side effects idempotent and support retry from the failed step without repeating completed actions.
Add rate limits, backoff, dead-letter handling, manual replay, cancellation, and secret rotation.
Ship Docker Compose, health checks, sample workflows, tests, backups, and connector-limit documentation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a broad connector marketplace.
Deliberately leave out unreviewed user code execution.
Deliberately leave out enterprise governance, guaranteed execution, and vendor-operated OAuth apps.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
